exercises.sentence: Where do we **meet** after work?

exercises.prompt: Match each Portuguese phrase with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: These are high-value chunks for everyday invitations and appointments. Several are best learned as whole phrases, not word by word.

pairs.support: Do you want to go for a coffee?
I have an appointment at ten.

exercises.prompt: Decline an invitation: say you can't today because you have a Portuguese class. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: To say you cannot do something, use «não posso». To give a reason about your own situation, use «tenho».
exercises.template: Hoje não ___, ___ aula de português.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap with the common fixed phrase.
exercises.explanation: «Fica para a próxima» is a ready-made way to say “maybe another time”. Learn it as one useful chunk.
exercises.template: Hoje não posso. ___ para a próxima.

exercises.prompt: At an office, say you have an appointment at ten. Fill the gap.
exercises.explanation: For an official booked time, use «marcação». This is the natural word in places like AIMA or Loja do Cidadão.
exercises.template: Tenho uma ___ às dez na Loja do Cidadão.

exercises.prompt: Two friends are fixing a time and place. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: Use «às» for clock times, and «da» in «o café da estação» because «de + a = da».
exercises.template: Pode ser ___ cinco no café ___ estação?

exercises.prompt: Say to your friend: "Do you want to go for a coffee this afternoon?"
exercises.explanation: With a friend, use the informal singular form «queres». «Esta tarde» means “this afternoon”.
acceptedAnswers: Tu queres ir tomar um café esta tarde?

exercises.prompt: Invite your friend: "Shall we go to the cinema on Saturday?"
exercises.explanation: A common suggestion is «Vamos ...?». Use the contractions «ao cinema» and «no sábado».
acceptedAnswers: Nós vamos ao cinema no sábado?

exercises.prompt: At a service desk, say politely: "I would like to book for tomorrow."
exercises.explanation: «Queria» is a polite fixed chunk very often used at desks and offices. Here the infinitive after it is «marcar».
acceptedAnswers: Eu queria marcar para amanhã.

exercises.prompt: Say to your friend: "Sorry, I can't, because I have to work."
exercises.explanation: Use «não posso» to decline, and «tenho de + infinitive» for obligation. «Porque» introduces the reason.
acceptedAnswers: Desculpa, não posso, porque tenho de trabalhar.
Desculpa, não posso porque eu tenho de trabalhar.

exercises.prompt: Say: "Let's meet at the metro station at six."
exercises.explanation: In an affirmative main clause, the pronoun goes after the verb: «Encontramo-nos». Also note «na estação» and «às seis».
acceptedAnswers: Nós encontramo-nos na estação de metro às seis.
Vamos encontrar-nos na estação de metro às seis.

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Sim, vamos!» Ask him (informal) if he wants to go to the cinema on Saturday.
exercises.explanation: To ask a friend, use the informal form «queres». The place and day need the contractions «ao» and «no».
acceptedAnswers: Tu queres ir ao cinema no sábado?

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Às seis.» Ask her (informal) what time to meet.
exercises.explanation: For clock time, ask with «A que horas». After a question expression, the pronoun comes before the verb: «nos encontramos».
acceptedAnswers: A que horas é que nos encontramos?
A que horas é que nós nos encontramos?

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Na estação de metro.» Ask him (informal) where to meet.
exercises.explanation: Ask about place with «Onde?» or «Onde é que ...?». In questions like this, Portuguese uses «nos encontramos».
acceptedAnswers: Onde é que nos encontramos?
Onde é que nós nos encontramos?

exercises.prompt: At the desk, the clerk answers: «Sim, pode ser.» Ask formally if tomorrow is possible for the appointment.
exercises.explanation: «Pode ser ...?» is a very common polite chunk for checking if a day or time works. Learn it as a whole phrase.
acceptedAnswers: Pode ser amanhã?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: After a question word, the clitic goes before the verb. For “we”, the correct pronoun is «nos»: «Onde nos encontramos?».

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With «ir a» + «o cinema», Portuguese makes the contraction «ao». So the natural phrase is «Vamos ao cinema».

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: Use a short natural reply to accept or decline, and you can add a time. For example: «Sim, pode ser às seis.» or «Desculpa, não posso.»
exercises.question: Queres ir tomar um café amanhã?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Sim, pode ser às seis.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Combinado!» closes an arrangement: “Agreed! / It’s settled!”. Use it once the time and place are fixed.
exercises.sentence: Six o'clock at the station? **Agreed**!

exercises.prompt: Invite your classmate (informal) to have lunch with you tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: For an informal invitation, Portuguese often uses «Queres + infinitive?». Here the activity is «almoçar» and «comigo» means “with me”.
acceptedAnswers: Tu queres almoçar comigo amanhã?

exercises.prompt: The receptionist answers: «No balcão 3.» Ask her (formal) at which desk you have the appointment.
exercises.explanation: To ask about the desk number, use «Em que balcão...?». The formal setting is in the situation, but the question is about you, so it uses «tenho».
acceptedAnswers: Em que balcão é que tenho a marcação?
Em que balcão é a minha marcação?

exercises.prompt: Arrange a place to meet. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: Use contractions with place nouns: «à porta» = a + a, and «da biblioteca» = de + a.
exercises.template: Podemos encontrar-nos ___ porta ___ biblioteca às cinco.

exercises.prompt: At the health centre desk, say politely: "I would like to change my appointment to Monday."
exercises.explanation: «Queria...» is a polite fixed chunk for requests. To say the new day, use «para» + day: «para segunda-feira».
acceptedAnswers: Eu queria mudar a minha marcação para segunda-feira.

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Às oito e meia, no restaurante.» Ask her (informal) where and at what time the dinner is.
exercises.explanation: You can ask for place and time in one question. In Portuguese, it is also natural to ask the time first and the place second.
exercises.givenAnswer: Às oito e meia, no restaurante.
acceptedAnswers: A que horas e onde é o jantar?
Onde e a que horas é que é o jantar?
Onde é o jantar e a que horas começa?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With this institution, Portuguese normally uses «nas Finanças» («em + as»). «No Finanças» is not the correct contraction.

exercises.prompt: At the desk, explain that you have an appointment but you cannot come at three. Fill the gaps.
exercises.explanation: Use «tenho» for something you have booked. To say you cannot come at that time, use «não posso».
exercises.template: Bom dia. ___ uma marcação, mas ___ posso às três.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: A simple answer is «Posso...» + time or day. You can also answer «Não posso...» and add a reason.
exercises.question: Quando podes?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Posso depois das seis.

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Porque tenho turnos ao sábado.» Ask him (informal) why he cannot come on Saturday.
exercises.explanation: To ask for a reason, use «Porque...?». The version with «é que» is also very common in Portugal.
acceptedAnswers: Porque é que não podes vir no sábado?

modules.title: Unit 6 — O corpo humano e saúde
modules.description: Describe how you feel and your symptoms, deal with the health centre and the pharmacy, and understand medical advice and instructions.

topics.title: Body, pain and symptoms
topics.context:
In health situations, you often need very practical phrases. In this topic, you learn body parts and simple ways to talk about pain and symptoms in Portugal.

- «Dói-me a cabeça.» — My head hurts.
- «Doem-me os pés.» — My feet hurt.
- «Dói-lhe o joelho.» — His/Her knee hurts. / Your knee hurts. (formal)
- «Sinto-me mal.» — I feel unwell.
- «Não me sinto bem.» — I don’t feel well.
- «Estou com febre e com tosse.» — I have a fever and a cough.
- «Tenho alergia.» — I have an allergy.
- «O que é que sente?» — What do you feel? (formal)

Watch out:

- With one body part, use «dói»: «Dói-me a cabeça.» With a plural body part, use «doem»: «Doem-me os pés.» / «Doem-lhe as costas.»
- In affirmative main clauses, the small pronoun usually comes after the verb: «dói-me», «doem-lhe», «sinto-me». After negation, it comes before: «não me sinto bem».
- Body parts normally use the article: «a cabeça», «os pés», «as costas».

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Cabeça» means 'head'. In this topic you will often use it with pain: «Dói-me a cabeça.»
exercises.sentence: My **head** hurts today.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Garganta» is 'throat'. It is a common word when you talk to a doctor or pharmacist.
exercises.sentence: The doctor looks at my **throat**.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: Portuguese usually uses the plural form «costas» for the body part 'back'.
exercises.sentence: After work, my **back** hurts.

exercises.prompt: Match each Portuguese sentence with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: These are useful ready-made phrases for describing pain and symptoms. Learn them as whole chunks.

exercises.prompt: You are describing how you feel today. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: Use «estar com» for symptoms like «febre», and «sentir-se» for your general feeling.
exercises.template: Hoje ___ com febre e ___ mal.

exercises.prompt: At the doctor. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: With «o senhor», the verb is in the 3rd person: «está». «A garganta» is singular, so use «dói-me».
exercises.template: O senhor ___ com tosse? — Sim, e ___-me a garganta.

exercises.prompt: After a long walk, fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: Use «doem» with a plural body part. «Os pés» is plural, so the verb must also be plural.
exercises.template: Quando caminho muito, ___-me os ___.

exercises.prompt: Li is ill. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: For «gripe» we practise «estar com». For «alergia» we use «ter».
exercises.template: A Li não se sente bem. Ela ___ com gripe e ___ alergia.

exercises.prompt: Say: My head hurts.
exercises.explanation: With one body part, use singular «dói». In an affirmative sentence, the pronoun comes after the verb: «dói-me».

exercises.prompt: Tell the doctor: My feet hurt.
exercises.explanation: «Os pés» is plural, so use «doem-me», not «dói-me».

exercises.prompt: Say that Ahmed has a cough.
exercises.explanation: A common pattern for symptoms is «estar com + noun»: «está com tosse». «Tem tosse» is also correct.
acceptedAnswers: Ahmed está com tosse.
O Ahmed tem tosse.
Ahmed tem tosse.

exercises.prompt: Say: I don't feel well.
exercises.explanation: After negation, the pronoun goes before the verb: «não me sinto».
acceptedAnswers: Eu não me sinto bem.

exercises.prompt: Say that Mariana has a headache.
exercises.explanation: A common fixed phrase is «ter dores de cabeça». Learn it as a whole chunk.
acceptedAnswers: Mariana tem dores de cabeça.
A Mariana está com dores de cabeça.

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Dói-me o joelho.» Ask him (informal) what hurts.
exercises.explanation: To ask informally about the painful body part, use «O que é que te dói?» with «te».
acceptedAnswers: O que te dói?

exercises.prompt: A patient answers: «Tenho alergia.» Ask her (formal) what she has.
exercises.explanation: In formal speech, ask with the 3rd-person verb: «tem».
acceptedAnswers: O que tem?
O que é que a senhora tem?

exercises.prompt: Your colleague answers: «Estou com febre.» Ask her (informal) if she has a fever.
exercises.explanation: For a yes/no question with «tu», use the 2nd-person form: «Estás com febre?»
acceptedAnswers: Tu estás com febre?
Tens febre?
Tu tens febre?

exercises.prompt: Your neighbour answers: «Sinto-me mal.» Ask him (formal) how he feels.
exercises.explanation: With formal «o senhor / a senhora», use the 3rd-person form: «Como se sente?»
acceptedAnswers: Como é que se sente?
Como é que o senhor se sente?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «As costas» is plural, so you need the plural verb: «doem-me».

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «O braço» is singular, so use «dói-me», not the plural form «doem-me».

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: You can answer with a symptom using «estar com / ter», or with a feeling using «sentir-se». A short combination is very natural.
exercises.question: O que é que sentes hoje?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Estou com tosse e sinto-me mal.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Neck» is «pescoço». In a full sentence, you normally use the article: «o pescoço».
exercises.sentence: My **neck** hurts when I work at the computer.

exercises.prompt: Match each body part with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: Body parts usually come with the article in Portuguese: «o braço», «a barriga». Learn the noun together with the article.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence.
exercises.explanation: Use «ter» with «alergia» and «estar com» with «gripe». They are two different patterns.
exercises.template: O Pedro ___ alergia e a irmã ___ com gripe.

exercises.prompt: Tell the doctor: my teeth hurt.
exercises.explanation: With a plural body part, use «doem». The article stays with the noun: «os dentes».

exercises.prompt: A patient answers: «Dói-me a perna.» Ask him formally where it hurts.
exercises.explanation: To ask about the place of pain, use «Onde». With formal singular, the pronoun is «lhe»: «Onde lhe dói?».
acceptedAnswers: Onde é que lhe dói?

exercises.prompt: At the clinic, the nurse tells the doctor about a male patient: His elbow hurts. (Use «lhe».)
exercises.explanation: With one body part, use «dói». «Lhe» means «to him / to her»; in an affirmative sentence it comes after the verb: «dói-lhe».

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence about a woman: at the end of the day, her eyes hurt.
exercises.explanation: «Olhos» is plural, so use «doem». In an affirmative sentence, the pronoun comes after the verb: «doem-lhe».
exercises.template: Ao fim do dia, ___ os ___.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «Joelho» is singular, so you need «dói». Use «doem» only with plural body parts such as «os olhos» or «os dentes».

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Sinto-me mal.» Ask her (informal) how she feels.
exercises.explanation: To ask about someone's state, use «Como te sentes?» with «tu». The verb is «sentir-se».
acceptedAnswers: Como é que te sentes?

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: Use «sentir-se» to say how you feel and add a symptom if you want. Any short true answer is fine.
exercises.question: Como te sentes hoje?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Sinto-me bem, só tenho alergia.

topics.title: Health centre, doctor and pharmacy
topics.context:
In Portugal, many everyday health needs start at the **centro de saúde**. There you can speak to reception, book a **consulta**, and use your **número de utente**. For health advice by phone, there is **SNS 24**. At the **farmácia**, some medicines are **sem receita** and others need a **receita médica**. Learn the most useful phrases as whole chunks.

- **Queria marcar uma consulta.** — I would like to make an appointment.
- **Quero desmarcar a consulta de amanhã.** — I want to cancel tomorrow’s appointment.
- **O meu número de utente é 12345678.** — My patient number is 12345678.
- **Preciso de análises ao sangue.** — I need blood tests.
- **Esta pomada precisa de receita?** — Does this ointment need a prescription?
- **Tome estes comprimidos de oito em oito horas.** — Take these tablets every eight hours.
- **Beba muita água e descanse.** — Drink plenty of water and rest.
- **Não se esqueça de ligar para o SNS 24.** — Don’t forget to call SNS 24.

**Watch out:**
- With staff, doctors and pharmacists, polite chunks like **Queria...** and **Pode repetir, por favor?** are very useful.
- Learn forms like **Tome**, **Beba** and **Descanse** as ready-made formal instructions to one person.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: In Portugal, «centro de saúde» is the local public health centre. You use it for appointments, nurses and your family doctor.
exercises.sentence: I have an appointment at the **health centre** tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Pediatra» is the doctor for children. «Enfermeiro» is a nurse, not a specialist doctor.
exercises.sentence: The child has an appointment with the **paediatrician**.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Receita médica» is a prescription from the doctor. At the pharmacy, people often shorten it to just «receita».
exercises.sentence: Do you have a **prescription** for this medicine?

exercises.prompt: Match each Portuguese health phrase with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: These are high-frequency health phrases. Learn them as whole chunks because you will hear them at the health centre and the pharmacy.

exercises.prompt: At the health centre, Ahmed wants to make an appointment with his family doctor. Fill the gap.
exercises.explanation: After «Queria», the usual chunk is «marcar uma consulta». «Médico de família» is your family doctor.
exercises.template: Queria ___ uma consulta com o médico de família.

exercises.prompt: At the pharmacy, the pharmacist asks about the medicine. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: At the pharmacy, people often shorten «receita médica» to «receita». «Sem receita» is a fixed phrase for medicines you can buy without a prescription.
exercises.template: Tem ___ médica ou é ___ receita?

exercises.prompt: The doctor gives two instructions. Fill the gaps.
exercises.explanation: Doctors often use short formal instructions to one person: «Beba», «Descanse», «Tome». Learn them as useful ready-made phrases.
exercises.template: ___ muita água e ___ em casa.

exercises.prompt: Complete the nurse's explanation.
exercises.explanation: «Análises ao sangue» is a fixed expression for blood tests. «Baixa médica» is sick leave certified by the doctor when you cannot work.
exercises.template: Precisa de ___ ao sangue e de uma ___ médica para faltar ao trabalho.

exercises.prompt: At the health centre, say politely (formal) that you want to make an appointment for tomorrow at 10.
exercises.explanation: «Queria...» is a polite fixed phrase for requests. Use «para amanhã às dez» to give the day and time.
acceptedAnswers: Eu queria marcar uma consulta para amanhã às dez.
Queria marcar uma consulta para amanhã às 10.
Eu queria marcar uma consulta para amanhã às 10.

exercises.prompt: At reception, say your patient number: my patient number is 12345678.
exercises.explanation: In European Portuguese, possessives normally take the article: «o meu número». At reception, this whole sentence is very useful.

exercises.prompt: At the pharmacy, ask politely (formal) if this ointment needs a prescription.
exercises.explanation: With medicines, «precisar de receita» asks if a prescription is needed. It is more natural than translating word by word from English.

exercises.prompt: Doctor's instruction to a patient (formal): Take these tablets every eight hours.
exercises.explanation: The doctor is giving a formal instruction to one patient, so the verb is «Tome». «De oito em oito horas» means every eight hours.
acceptedAnswers: Tome estes comprimidos de 8 em 8 horas.

exercises.prompt: Doctor's instruction to a patient (formal): Don't forget to call SNS 24.
exercises.explanation: After negation, the pronoun comes before the verb: «Não se esqueça». Learn this whole phrase as a polite formal instruction.
acceptedAnswers: Não se esqueça de ligar ao SNS 24.

exercises.prompt: Your classmate answers: «Às onze.» Ask him (informal) what time his appointment is.
exercises.explanation: For time, use «A que horas...?». With a friend, the verb is «tens».
acceptedAnswers: A que horas é que tens consulta?
A que horas é a tua consulta?
A que horas é que é a tua consulta?
A que horas tens a consulta?
A que horas é que tens a consulta?

exercises.prompt: Your neighbour answers: «É no centro de saúde da Alameda.» Ask her (informal) where the appointment is.
exercises.explanation: Use «Onde é que...?» to ask where something is. «Consulta» is feminine, so you say «a consulta».
exercises.givenAnswer: É no centro de saúde da Alameda.
acceptedAnswers: Onde é a consulta?
Onde é a tua consulta?
Onde é que é a tua consulta?
Onde tens consulta?
Onde é que tens consulta?

exercises.prompt: The pharmacist answers: «Não, é sem receita.» Ask him (formal) whether this syrup needs a prescription.
exercises.explanation: At the pharmacy, «precisar de receita» is the normal way to ask about a prescription. «Sem receita» is the answer if you can buy it directly.
acceptedAnswers: É preciso receita para este xarope?
Este xarope é com receita?

exercises.prompt: The receptionist answers: «É o 808 24 24 24.» Ask her (formal) what the SNS 24 number is.
exercises.explanation: Use «Qual é o número...?» to ask for a phone number. «Do SNS 24» is «de + o» → «do».
acceptedAnswers: Qual é o número de telefone do SNS 24?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «Consulta» is feminine, so the article must be «uma». «Um consulta» is a gender mistake.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With «ir», European Portuguese uses the preposition «a»: «vou ao centro de saúde» (a + o = ao). «Vou no» is not correct here.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: SNS 24 is for health advice by phone when it is not an emergency. Answer with your own reason or situation.
exercises.question: Quando é que ligas para o SNS 24?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Ligo quando tenho febre alta.

exercises.prompt: At reception, say politely that you want to cancel Friday's appointment.
exercises.explanation: «Queria...» is a very useful polite chunk with staff. Use «desmarcar» for cancelling an appointment.
acceptedAnswers: Eu queria desmarcar a consulta de sexta-feira.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gaps: at the health centre, the nurse measures blood pressure and the family doctor does the consultation.
exercises.explanation: At the health centre, «o enfermeiro» can do checks like blood pressure, and «o médico de família» is the family doctor.
exercises.template: No centro de saúde, o ___ mede a tensão e o ___ de família faz a consulta.

exercises.prompt: The receptionist answers: «Para terça-feira.» Ask her (formal) when the appointment is.
exercises.explanation: To ask about the scheduled day, you can say «Para quando é a consulta?». A shorter common form is «Quando é a consulta?».
acceptedAnswers: Quando é a consulta?
Quando é que é a consulta?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «Receita» is feminine, so the adjective must also be feminine: «médica».

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «O penso» is a bandage or dressing. «A pomada» is ointment that you put on the skin.
exercises.sentence: I need a **bandage** for my finger.

exercises.prompt: At the pharmacy, ask politely for cough syrup.
exercises.explanation: At a pharmacy, «Queria...» is a polite way to ask for something. «Xarope para a tosse» is a useful ready-made chunk.
acceptedAnswers: Queria um xarope para a tosse por favor.
Eu queria um xarope para a tosse, por favor.
Eu queria um xarope para a tosse por favor.

exercises.prompt: The pharmacist answers: «É sem receita.» Ask the pharmacist if this syrup is without prescription.
exercises.explanation: Use the chunk «sem receita» for medicine that you can buy without a prescription.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two gaps in the doctor's instruction.
exercises.explanation: These are common ready-made instructions: «tomar» with medicine like syrup, and «beber» with water.
exercises.template: O médico diz: «Tome o ___ depois do jantar e beba muita ___.»

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: You can answer personally. With phone services, Portuguese uses «ligar para».
exercises.question: Quando estás doente, ligas para o SNS 24?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Sim, ligo para o SNS 24.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «Penso» is masculine, so you say «um penso». The article must match the noun.

topics.title: Healthy habits and advice
topics.context:
To give simple advice in Portuguese, three patterns are very common.

- `Deves beber mais água.` = “You should drink more water.”
- `Tens de descansar.` = “You have to rest.”
- `É melhor dormir cedo.` = “It is better to sleep early.”
- `Pratica desporto todos os dias.` = “Do exercise every day.” (to one friend)
- `Pratique desporto todos os dias.` = “Do exercise every day.” (formal: to one patient or client)
- `Não fumes.` = “Don’t smoke.” (informal)
- `Não fume.` = “Don’t smoke.” (formal)

Frequency is very useful with health routines: `todos os dias` = every day, `duas vezes por semana` = twice a week, `de oito em oito horas` = every eight hours.

**Watch out:** with **tu**, statements use `deves / tens de`. The positive imperative looks like the ele/ela present form, without -s: `come / dorme / pratica` (not `comes / dormes / praticas`). The negative is different: `não comas`, `não fumes`. With formal advice (`o senhor / a senhora`), use 3rd-person forms: `deve`, `coma`, `durma`, `não fume`.

exercises.prompt: Tell your friend: You should drink more water.
exercises.explanation: With informal singular, use `deves` + infinitive. Portuguese often drops the subject pronoun `tu`.
acceptedAnswers: Tu deves beber mais água.

exercises.prompt: Give formal advice to one patient: Sleep eight hours.
exercises.explanation: For formal advice to one person, the imperative uses the 3rd-person form: `durma`.

exercises.prompt: Tell a friend not to smoke.
exercises.explanation: Negative informal advice uses `não` + the informal imperative form here: `não fumes`.

exercises.prompt: Say: It is better to rest today.
exercises.explanation: After `é melhor`, Portuguese normally uses the infinitive: `descansar`.

exercises.prompt: Tell your friend: You have to take this medicine every eight hours.
exercises.explanation: `Ter de` + infinitive expresses necessity. `De oito em oito horas` is the fixed phrase for regular intervals of eight hours.
acceptedAnswers: Tu tens de tomar este medicamento de oito em oito horas.

exercises.prompt: Give informal advice: Eat fruit every day.
exercises.explanation: For «tu», the affirmative imperative looks like the ele/ela present form, without -s: «come» (not «comes»). Frequency phrases like «todos os dias» often come at the end.

exercises.prompt: The doctor answers: «Deve beber mais água.» Ask the doctor (formal) what you should drink.
exercises.explanation: To ask about a thing, use `O que`. With `dever`, the next verb stays in the infinitive.
acceptedAnswers: O que é que devo beber?
O que é que eu devo beber?

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Tens de dormir mais.» Ask your friend (informal) what you have to do.
exercises.explanation: Use `O que` to ask for the action. With `ter de`, the main verb after `de` is an infinitive.
acceptedAnswers: O que é que tenho de fazer?
O que é que eu tenho de fazer?

exercises.prompt: The nurse answers: «É melhor descansar hoje.» Ask the nurse (formal) if it is better for you to rest today.
exercises.explanation: A yes/no question can keep the same word order and use question intonation. `É melhor` is followed by the infinitive.
acceptedAnswers: É melhor eu descansar hoje?

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Duas vezes por semana.» Ask him (informal) how often he does exercise.
exercises.explanation: `Quantas vezes por semana` is the natural way to ask about weekly frequency. With `tu`, the verb is `fazes`.
acceptedAnswers: Quantas vezes por semana é que fazes exercício?
Quantas vezes por semana é que tu fazes exercício?
Quantas vezes por semana fazes desporto?
Quantas vezes por semana é que fazes desporto?

exercises.prompt: The pharmacist answers: «De oito em oito horas.» Ask the pharmacist (formal) how often you take the medicine.
exercises.explanation: `Com que frequência` asks about regularity. The answer uses the fixed interval expression `de oito em oito horas`.
acceptedAnswers: Com que frequência é que tomo o medicamento?
Com que frequência é que eu tomo o medicamento?
De quantas em quantas horas tomo o medicamento?

exercises.prompt: You are giving simple health advice. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: After `dever`, use the infinitive. With `tu`, the correct form is `deves`.
exercises.template: Se estás cansado, ___ dormir mais e ___ mais água.

exercises.prompt: A nutritionist is speaking formally to Dona Ana. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: Formal imperative uses 3rd-person forms. In negative advice, `não` comes before the verb: `não fume`.
exercises.template: Dona Ana, ___ fruta todos os dias e não ___.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gaps: I exercise twice a week and drink water every day.
exercises.explanation: These are fixed time expressions. `Duas vezes por semana` gives weekly frequency, and `todos os dias` means every day.
exercises.template: Faço exercício ___ por semana e bebo água ___ os dias.

exercises.prompt: You are advising a friend about sleep. Fill the three gaps.
exercises.explanation: After `tens de` and after `é melhor`, Portuguese uses the infinitive. So the second and third gaps are not conjugated forms.
exercises.template: Para dormir melhor, ___ de jantar cedo e ___ mais. Também é melhor não ___ café à noite.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With `tu`, the verb `dever` changes to `deves`. `Deve` is the form for ele/ela/você/o senhor/a senhora.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With formal address like `Senhor João`, the negative imperative uses the 3rd-person form: `não fume`.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: For one formal person, `should` is often expressed with `deve` in this topic.
exercises.sentence: You (formal) **should** drink more water.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the words in bold.
exercises.explanation: `De oito em oito horas` is a common fixed phrase for medicine and other regular intervals.
exercises.sentence: Take this medicine **every eight hours**.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: Use the present to talk about your real routine. One or two short healthy habits are enough.
exercises.question: O que fazes para ter hábitos saudáveis?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Como fruta e durmo oito horas.

exercises.prompt: Tell your friend: You should go to bed early.
exercises.explanation: With informal singular, «dever» is «deves». After «deves», use the infinitive, and the reflexive pronoun stays attached: «deitar-te».
acceptedAnswers: Tu deves deitar-te cedo.
Deves-te deitar cedo.
Deves ir para a cama cedo.

exercises.prompt: A doctor answers: «Duas vezes por semana.» Ask formally how often you should walk.
exercises.explanation: To ask about frequency, use «Com que frequência». When you ask the doctor for advice about yourself, the verb is in the 1st person: «devo caminhar».
acceptedAnswers: Com que frequência é que devo caminhar?
Quantas vezes por semana devo caminhar?

exercises.prompt: You are giving advice about stress. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: «É melhor + infinitive» is a common pattern for advice. When two verbs follow it with «e», both stay in the infinitive: «falar» e «descansar».
exercises.template: Se tens muito stress, ___ falar com o médico e ___ mais.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: After «deve», Portuguese uses the infinitive: «deve descansar». «Descansas» is a present-tense form, not the infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: A common healthy-eating phrase is «fruta e legumes». In European Portuguese, «legumes» here means vegetables.
exercises.sentence: You should eat more **vegetables**.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: Use the present to describe your own routine or habits. One or two short actions are enough.
exercises.question: O que fazes para dormir melhor?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Janto cedo e desligo o telemóvel.

exercises.prompt: Give formal advice to one patient: do not drink coffee at night.
exercises.explanation: For formal negative advice, use «não» + the 3rd-person form: «não beba». «À noite» is the usual time expression here.

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «É melhor desligar o telemóvel.» Ask him (informal) what is better to do before sleeping.
exercises.explanation: To ask for advice with «é melhor», you can say «O que é melhor fazer...?». «Antes de dormir» gives the exact moment you are asking about.
acceptedAnswers: Antes de dormir, o que é melhor fazer?
O que é que é melhor fazer antes de dormir?

exercises.prompt: You are advising Miguel. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: With «tu», the positive command is «bebe», but negative advice is «não bebas». Learn this pair as a fixed imperative pattern.
exercises.template: Miguel, ___ mais água e não ___ tantas bebidas com açúcar.

exercises.prompt: Give general advice: It is better to eat soup and salad at dinner.
exercises.explanation: «É melhor + infinitive» gives neutral advice without saying who the person is. «Ao jantar» is the normal expression for ‘at dinner’.

modules.title: Unit 7 — Eu e o mundo do trabalho
modules.description: Look for work, apply and attend an interview, understand contracts and working conditions, and talk about past work with the Pretérito Perfeito.

topics.title: Looking for a job, CV and interview
topics.context:
Looking for a job in Portugal often starts with an **anúncio de trabalho** or **oferta de emprego**. You usually send a **candidatura** with your **currículo (CV)** and sometimes a **carta de apresentação**. In an interview, short formal questions are very common, so it helps to learn them as ready-made phrases.

- «Procuro emprego na área da logística.» — “I’m looking for work in logistics.”
- «Queria candidatar-me a esta oferta de emprego.» — “I would like to apply for this job offer.”
- «Aqui está o meu currículo.» — “Here is my CV.”
- «Tenho experiência profissional na restauração.» — “I have work experience in hospitality / restaurant work.”
- «Tenho carta de condução.» — “I have a driving licence.”
- «Que experiência tem?» — “What experience do you have?”
- «Fala inglês?» — “Do you speak English?”
- «Tem disponibilidade para trabalhar ao fim de semana?» — “Are you available to work at weekends?”

**Watch out:**
- In formal interview questions, use 3rd-person forms: «tem», «fala», not «tens», «falas».
- Many useful nouns come from verbs: «candidatar-se → candidatura», «inscrever-se → inscrição», «marcar → marcação», «informar → informação». Many end in **-ção**. Learn the verb and noun together.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Anúncio de trabalho» is a job ad. «Candidatura» is your application, and «entrevista de trabalho» is the interview.
exercises.sentence: I saw a **job ad** online this morning.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: In Portugal, «currículo» is the full word for CV or résumé. In everyday use, people also say «CV».
exercises.sentence: Please send your **résumé** and your contact details.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Disponibilidade» means availability. In job ads, it often appears with time expressions such as «ao fim de semana».
exercises.sentence: The job requires weekend **availability**.

exercises.prompt: Match each work sector with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: These sector names often appear in job ads and in CVs. Learn them as whole chunks.

exercises.prompt: Raj is talking about his plans. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: After «querer», use the infinitive: «quero procurar». The common chunk for a job offer is «oferta de emprego».
exercises.template: Quero ___ emprego. Há uma ___ de emprego no jornal.

exercises.prompt: Complete the two words from the same family.
exercises.explanation: The verb is «candidatar-se a». The related noun is «candidatura» (with -ura, not -ção).
exercises.template: Quero ___-me a esta oferta. A minha ___ está pronta.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gaps: you need an appointment at the health centre and more information about the opening hours.
exercises.explanation: These useful service nouns end in «-ção»: «marcação» and «informação». They are common in offices and health services.
exercises.template: Preciso de uma ___ no centro de saúde e de mais ___ sobre o horário.

exercises.prompt: Complete this sentence about a CV.
exercises.explanation: In a CV, «habilitações académicas» is your studies or qualifications, and «experiência profissional» is your work experience.
exercises.template: No meu CV, escrevo as minhas ___ académicas e a minha ___ profissional.

exercises.prompt: You are writing to a company. Say politely that you want to apply for this job offer.
exercises.explanation: After the polite chunk «Queria», the reflexive stays attached to the infinitive: «candidatar-me». This verb takes «a»: «candidatar-se a uma oferta».
acceptedAnswers: Eu queria candidatar-me a esta oferta de emprego.

exercises.prompt: In an interview, say that you have a driving licence.
exercises.explanation: Portuguese uses the fixed expression «carta de condução» for driving licence. You can omit «eu» because «tenho» already shows the subject.
acceptedAnswers: Eu tenho carta de condução.

exercises.prompt: Say that you work in the cleaning sector.
exercises.explanation: For sectors, «trabalhar em» + area is the normal pattern: «em limpezas», «em saúde», «em logística».
acceptedAnswers: Eu trabalho em limpezas.

exercises.prompt: In a job interview, say that you speak English and Portuguese.
exercises.explanation: With no subject pronoun, «falo» already means «I speak». Languages are linked with «e».
acceptedAnswers: Eu falo inglês e português.

exercises.prompt: Say that you are available to work at the weekend.
exercises.explanation: The chunk is «ter disponibilidade para» + infinitive. In general statements, Portuguese often says «ao fim de semana».
acceptedAnswers: Eu tenho disponibilidade para trabalhar ao fim de semana.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: «Quero trabalhar em/na + sector» is a simple way to say the area you want. Some sectors take a contraction, for example «na saúde».
exercises.question: Em que área queres trabalhar?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Quero trabalhar na saúde.

exercises.prompt: The candidate answers: «Tenho experiência na restauração.» Ask in the formal register what experience the candidate has.
exercises.explanation: Formal singular uses 3rd-person forms: «tem». You can also hear the emphatic version «Que experiência é que tem?».
acceptedAnswers: Que experiência é que tem?

exercises.prompt: The candidate answers: «Sim, falo inglês.» Ask in a job interview, in the formal register, if the candidate speaks English.
exercises.explanation: In formal questions, Portuguese often uses just the verb in 3rd person: «Fala inglês?». «O senhor / A senhora» is possible but not necessary.
acceptedAnswers: O senhor fala inglês?
A senhora fala inglês?

exercises.prompt: The candidate answers: «Tenho disponibilidade ao fim de semana.» Ask in the formal register if the candidate is available to work at weekends.
exercises.explanation: The formal verb is «tem». Both the longer question with «para trabalhar» and the shorter version are natural.
exercises.givenAnswer: Tenho disponibilidade ao fim de semana.
acceptedAnswers: Tem disponibilidade ao fim de semana?

exercises.prompt: The candidate answers: «Tenho carta de condução.» Ask in the formal register if the candidate has a driving licence.
exercises.explanation: Again, formal singular uses 3rd-person «tem». «Carta de condução» is the standard expression in Portugal.
acceptedAnswers: O senhor tem carta de condução?
A senhora tem carta de condução?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong for a formal interview. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With a candidate you do not know well, formal singular uses 3rd-person forms: «tem». «Tens» is the informal «tu» form.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: After «preciso de mais», you need a noun here: «informação». «Informar» is the verb.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: For job applications, «carta de apresentação» means a cover letter. Do not confuse it with «carta de condução», which is a driving licence.
exercises.sentence: Please attach a **cover letter** to your application.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: Some work sectors are best learned as fixed expressions. In Portuguese, «construction sector» is «construção civil».
exercises.sentence: He wants to work in the **construction sector**.

exercises.prompt: Complete the noun forms.
exercises.explanation: Learn the verb and noun together: «candidatar-se → candidatura», «inscrever-se → inscrição», «informar → informação». Many of these nouns end in «-ção».
exercises.template: candidatar-se → ___ ; inscrever-se → ___ ; informar → ___.

exercises.prompt: You are preparing a job application. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: A job application often includes the CV and a cover letter. «Currículo» is also often called «CV».
exercises.template: Na candidatura, junto o meu ___ e a minha ___.

exercises.prompt: Say that you have a job interview tomorrow morning.
exercises.explanation: Use «ter» for scheduled events: «Tenho uma entrevista...». «Entrevista de trabalho» is the fixed phrase for a job interview.
acceptedAnswers: Eu tenho uma entrevista de trabalho amanhã de manhã.

exercises.prompt: Say that you send your CV and your cover letter.
exercises.explanation: With possessives in European Portuguese, use the article: «o meu currículo», «a minha carta». This is a useful sentence for talking about your application documents.
acceptedAnswers: Eu envio o meu currículo e a minha carta de apresentação.
Envio o meu CV e a minha carta de apresentação.
Eu envio o meu CV e a minha carta de apresentação.

exercises.prompt: The candidate answers: «Tenho o 12.º ano.» Ask him formally about his educational qualifications.
exercises.explanation: In a formal interview, use the 3rd-person form «tem». «Habilitações académicas» is the usual phrase for educational qualifications.
acceptedAnswers: Que habilitações académicas é que tem?
Quais são as suas habilitações académicas?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: After «disponibilidade», Portuguese uses «para» + infinitive: «disponibilidade para trabalhar». «Por trabalhar» does not fit here.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «Habilitações» is plural feminine, so the possessive must agree: «as minhas». In European Portuguese, the article stays before the possessive.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: You can answer with «Procuro trabalho» or «Procuro emprego» plus a sector. Use the area that is true for you.
exercises.question: Em que área procuras emprego?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Procuro trabalho na agricultura.

topics.title: Contracts and working conditions
topics.context:
When you start a job in Portugal, you need practical words for the contract, the hours, the pay and the deductions. In real life, you often ask short, direct questions and read simple documents such as the contract or the **recibo de vencimento**.

- `Tenho um contrato a termo certo.` = I have a fixed-term contract.
- `Tenho um contrato sem termo.` = I have a permanent contract.
- `O período experimental é de trinta dias.` = The probation period is thirty days.
- `Trabalho a tempo inteiro, das nove às dezoito.` = I work full-time, from 9 to 6.
- `No recibo de vencimento vejo o salário e os descontos para a Segurança Social.` = On the payslip I see the salary and the Social Security deductions.
- `Quantos dias de férias tenho?` = How many holiday days do I have?
- `Há subsídio de refeição?` = Is there a meal allowance?

**Watch out:** in Portugal, `salário` and `ordenado` are both common in everyday speech; `remuneração` is a bit more formal. Learn `Queria saber...` as a polite fixed phrase for questions to an employer.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: In Portugal, a permanent job contract is called «contrato sem termo». It is different from «contrato a termo certo», which has an end date.
exercises.sentence: I have a **permanent contract**.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: A meal allowance is «subsídio de refeição». It is a fixed phrase you often hear at work in Portugal.
exercises.sentence: There is **meal allowance** in this job.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Turnos» means shifts. The common expression is «trabalhar por turnos».
exercises.sentence: I work in **shifts**.

exercises.prompt: Match each Portuguese work term with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: These are very common words in contracts and job conversations. Learn them as useful chunks, not as isolated grammar.

exercises.prompt: Complete the fixed expression for a fixed-term contract with a set end date.
exercises.explanation: The full expression is «contrato a termo certo». Only «sem termo» means a permanent contract.
exercises.template: Tenho um contrato ___ termo ___.

exercises.prompt: Complete the name of the institution in the sentence.
exercises.explanation: In Portugal, the institution is «a Segurança Social». After «para», the article stays: «para a Segurança Social».
exercises.template: No recibo de vencimento vejo os descontos para a ___ ___.

exercises.prompt: Say: I have a permanent contract.
exercises.explanation: Use the fixed phrase «contrato sem termo» for a permanent contract. In European Portuguese, you can say it with or without «eu».
acceptedAnswers: Eu tenho um contrato sem termo.

exercises.prompt: Say politely to your employer: I would like to see my payslip, please.
exercises.explanation: «Queria...» is a polite fixed chunk for requests. «Payslip» is «recibo de vencimento».
acceptedAnswers: Eu queria ver o meu recibo de vencimento, por favor.

exercises.prompt: Your employer answers: «Das nove às dezoito.» Ask in a formal way what the working hours are.
exercises.explanation: To ask about working hours, use «Qual é o horário?» or the longer «Qual é o horário de trabalho?». Both are natural in Portugal.
acceptedAnswers: Qual é o horário de trabalho?

exercises.prompt: Your employer answers: «Tem vinte e dois dias por ano.» Ask in a formal way how many holiday days you have.
exercises.explanation: Ask about your own holiday entitlement with «Quantos dias de férias tenho?». The version with «é que» is also very common.
exercises.givenAnswer: Tem vinte e dois dias por ano.
acceptedAnswers: Quantos dias de férias é que tenho?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «Turno» is masculine: «o turno, os turnos». The fixed expression is «por turnos».

exercises.prompt: Say: I work full-time and I have Sunday off.
exercises.explanation: Use «a tempo inteiro» for full-time. For a regular weekly day off, Portuguese often uses «ao domingo».
acceptedAnswers: Eu trabalho a tempo inteiro e tenho folga ao domingo.
Trabalho a tempo inteiro e tenho folga aos domingos.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the names of the Christmas bonus and the holiday bonus.
exercises.explanation: In Portugal, these common payments are «subsídio de Natal» and «subsídio de férias». They are fixed expressions.
exercises.template: Na empresa há subsídio de ___ e subsídio de ___.

exercises.prompt: Your employer answers: «Sim, há subsídio de refeição.» Ask in a formal way if there is a meal allowance.
exercises.explanation: A simple yes/no question is enough here: «Há subsídio de refeição?». «Existe...» is also possible.
acceptedAnswers: Existe subsídio de refeição?

exercises.prompt: At a job interview. Put the lines in order.
exercises.explanation: A polite conversation often starts with a greeting, then the applicant asks a short question. «Qual é o horário de trabalho?» is a ready-made useful question.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bom dia. Sim, qual é o horário de trabalho?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Das nove às dezoito, com uma hora de almoço.

exercises.prompt: Ask politely: I would like to know what the salary is.
exercises.explanation: «Queria saber...» is a useful polite chunk for talking to an employer. In everyday Portuguese, «salário» and «ordenado» are both common.
acceptedAnswers: Eu queria saber qual é o salário.
Queria saber qual é o ordenado.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: I work under a service arrangement and I use green receipts.
exercises.explanation: In Portugal, self-employed work is often called «prestação de serviços». The common phrase is «recibos verdes».
exercises.template: Trabalho em regime de ___ e passo recibos ___.

exercises.prompt: Your employer answers: «Sim, os descontos são para a Segurança Social.» Ask in a formal way if the deductions are for Social Security.
exercises.explanation: This question checks the destination of the deductions. The institution name is «a Segurança Social», so the question uses «para a».
exercises.givenAnswer: Sim, os descontos são para a Segurança Social.
acceptedAnswers: São para a Segurança Social os descontos?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «Segurança Social» is feminine: «a Segurança Social». After «para», we say «para a Segurança Social».

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: You can answer with exact hours, or more generally with a pattern such as «Trabalho por turnos». Keep it short and natural.
exercises.question: Qual é o teu horário de trabalho?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Trabalho das oito às dezassete.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: In Portugal, the usual word for a payslip is «recibo de vencimento». You often need this document for the bank or for other paperwork.
exercises.sentence: I need my **payslip** for the bank.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: For a full-time job, Portuguese normally uses the fixed expression «a tempo inteiro».
exercises.sentence: This job is **full-time**.

exercises.prompt: You are reading a contract. Fill the gaps: In the contract I see the probation period and the working hours.
exercises.explanation: A contract can show both the probation period and the working hours. These are common things to check before you start.
exercises.template: No contrato vejo o ___ e o ___.

exercises.prompt: Ana works only four hours a day. Fill the gap.
exercises.explanation: In Portugal, «part-time» is very common in everyday speech. It contrasts with «a tempo inteiro».
exercises.template: A Ana trabalha só quatro horas por dia; é um trabalho ___.

exercises.prompt: Say: This company offers a fixed-term contract.
exercises.explanation: Use «oferece» for what a company gives, and the fixed expression is «contrato a termo certo».

topics.title: Talking about past work: Pretérito Perfeito
topics.context:
Use the **Pretérito Perfeito Simples** for actions that are finished in the past, especially with clear time markers such as **ontem**, **no ano passado**, **há dois anos** and **durante três anos**. In real life in Portugal, you use it a lot to talk about past jobs, courses and important steps in your work history.

- **Ontem trabalhei até às seis.** — Yesterday I worked until six.
- **No ano passado, a Fátima trabalhou num hotel.** — Last year Fátima worked in a hotel.
- **Há dois anos, vim para Portugal.** — I came to Portugal two years ago.
- **Trabalhámos numa fábrica durante três anos.** — We worked in a factory for three years.
- **Comecei um curso e aprendi muito.** — I started a course and learned a lot.
- **Ele fez um estágio e depois foi para outra empresa.** — He did an internship and then went to another company.

**Watch out:** some verbs are irregular: **fiz, disse, vim, tive, fui**. Also, some **eu** forms change spelling to keep the sound: **fiquei, cheguei, comecei, paguei**.

In European Portuguese, the subject pronoun is often dropped: **Trabalhei num café** is more natural than **Eu trabalhei num café**, but both are correct.

topics.title: Past habits and descriptions: Pretérito Imperfeito
topics.context:
The **Pretérito Imperfeito** is used to describe continuous past states, habits, routines, and background circumstances ("used to do", "was doing"). In Portugal, it is also frequently used to make polite requests.

### Regular Endings
- **-ar verbs** (*morar*): *eu morava, tu moravas, ele/ela/você morava, nós morávamos, vocês/eles/elas moravam*
- **-er / -ir verbs** (*viver, sair*): *eu vivia, tu vivias, ele/ela/você vivia, nós vivíamos, vocês/eles/elas viviam*

### Essential Irregular Verbs
- **ser**: *era, eras, era, éramos, eram*
- **ter**: *tinha, tinhas, tinha, tínhamos, tinham*
- **vir**: *vinha, vinhas, vinha, vínhamos, vinham*
- **pôr**: *punha, punhas, punha, púnhamos, punham*

### Examples
- *Quando era jovem, vivia no campo.* (When I was young, I lived in the countryside.)
- *Antigamente, a Fátima trabalhava numa fábrica.* (Formerly, Fátima worked in a factory.)
- *Nós tínhamos muitos amigos na escola.* (We had many friends at school.)
- *Gostava de pedir um comprovativo de morada.* (I would like to request a proof of address — polite imperfect chunk).

### Watch Out
1. **Tu vs. Você forms**: Make sure to use the correct ending for *tu* (*-avas / -ias*) versus formal/3rd person (*-ava / -ia*).
2. **Definite Articles**: Always include articles before possessives in European Portuguese (*os meus amigos*, *a sua profissão*).

topics.title: Pretérito Perfeito vs Imperfeito
topics.context:
In European Portuguese, choosing between the **Pretérito Perfeito Simples** and the **Pretérito Imperfeito** depends on how you view the past action:

1. **Pretérito Perfeito**: Used for completed, punctual actions or events that happened at a specific moment in time.
   - *No ano passado mudei-me para Portugal.* (Last year I moved to Portugal.)
   - *Ontem fui às Finanças e tratei do NIF.* (Yesterday I went to Finanças and sorted out my NIF.)

2. **Pretérito Imperfeito**: Used for past habits, repeated actions, ongoing background states, descriptions, age, and feelings.
   - *Antigamente trabalhava num banco.* (In the past I used to work in a bank.)
   - *Quando cheguei, não falava português.* (When I arrived, I didn't speak Portuguese.)

**Common Time Markers:**
- **Perfeito**: *ontem, na semana passada, em 2020, no ano passado, há X anos* (for a single event: *Há três anos cheguei a Lisboa*).
- **Imperfeito**: *antigamente, dantes, quando era criança, normalmente, todos os dias*.

**Watch out:** Sentences often combine both tenses! The Imperfeito describes the background state or ongoing action, while the Perfeito introduces a specific event that interrupted or happened during that time (*Quando vivia em Lisboa, comprei um carro*).

topics.title: Life stages, migration and changes
topics.context:
When talking about your life story in Portugal, you often contrast past habits with your current routine, or talk about migration memories. To describe past habits or situations, use **Antigamente** (in the past / back then) or **No meu país** (in my country) with the Pretérito Imperfeito (*vivia*, *falava*, *fazia*). To speak about your current life, use **Hoje em dia** (nowadays) or **Agora** (now) with the Presente (*moro*, *falo*, *faço*).

Examples:
- *Antigamente vivia na Alemanha, mas hoje em dia moro em Portugal.* (In the past I lived in Germany, but nowadays I live in Portugal.)
- *No meu país fazia muito frio.* (In my country it was very cold.)
- *Há cinco anos não falava português, mas hoje já compreendo muito bem.* (Five years ago I didn't speak Portuguese, but today I understand very well.)
- *Tenho saudades da minha terra natal.* (I miss my hometown.)

**Watch out:** In European Portuguese, expressing nostalgia uses **ter saudades de** followed by a definite article: *Tenho saudades **da** minha família* (never leave out the article!). To express how long ago something happened, use **há + time**: *Cheguei a Portugal **há** três anos*.

topics.title: Opinions, agreement and disagreement
topics.context:
Expressing your point of view, agreeing, disagreeing, and making cultural comparisons are essential social skills in Portugal.

### Expressing an Opinion
* **Acho que...** (I think that...): *Acho que Portugal é um país tranquilo.*
* **Na minha opinião,...** (In my opinion,...): *Na minha opinião, a burocracia é difícil.*
* **Para mim,...** (For me,...): *Para mim, o clima em Lisboa é ótimo.*

### Agreeing & Disagreeing
* **Concordo contigo!** (I agree with you! - informal)
* **Concordo com o senhor / a senhora.** (I agree with you - formal)
* **Tens razão. / Tem razão.** (You are right. - informal / formal)
* **Não concordo com isso.** (I don't agree with that.)
* **Não é bem assim.** (It's not quite like that.)
* **Depende.** (It depends.)

### Comparing Cultures
* **No meu país é diferente porque...** (In my country it is different because...)
* **É mais... do que...** (It is more... than...)
* **É menos... do que...** (It is less... than...)

> **Watch out!** Always include the definite article before possessives in European Portuguese (*a minha opinião*, *no meu país*).

topics.title: News, society and community life
topics.context:
**In this topic** you talk about short news texts and about community life in Portugal. You learn words for parts of a news item (*notícia, título, artigo, gráfico, entrevista*) and for social life (*comunidade, vizinhos, associação, voluntariado*). You also practise two very common patterns in simple news Portuguese: **Segundo a notícia...** (*According to the news item...*) and **O número de ... aumentou / diminuiu** (*The number of ... increased / decreased*).

Examples:
- **Leio o título primeiro.** — *I read the headline first.*
- **Este artigo fala de integração.** — *This article talks about integration.*
- **Há um gráfico no jornal.** — *There is a graph in the newspaper.*
- **Os vizinhos participam na associação do bairro.** — *The neighbours take part in the neighbourhood association.*
- **Faço voluntariado ao sábado.** — *I do voluntary work on Saturdays.*
- **Segundo a notícia, o número de voluntários aumentou.** — *According to the news item, the number of volunteers increased.*

Watch out:
- After **o número de**, the verb is usually singular: **o número de alunos aumentou**.
- **Direitos e deveres** is a fixed chunk: learn it together as “rights and duties”.

exercises.explanation: After «ajudar», Portuguese often uses «a + infinitive»: «ajuda ... a aprender».

exercises.explanation: In European Portuguese, possessives before a noun take the article: «os nossos vizinhos». «Na» is «em + a».

exercises.explanation: To ask for the thing someone reads, use «O que». In European Portuguese, «é que» is also very common.

exercises.explanation: After «o número de ...», the verb is usually singular. So we say «o número de pessoas aumentou».

exercises.explanation: «Gráfico» goes with the masculine article «um», and «entrevista» goes with the feminine article «uma».
exercises.template: No jornal, há um ___ e uma ___ sobre a comunidade.

exercises.explanation: Use «Onde» to ask about place. In European Portuguese, the question can be «Onde é que ...?»

exercises.sentence: It is important to know your **rights and duties** in Portugal.

topics.title: Holidays, traditions and celebrations
topics.context:
In this topic you learn vocabulary for holidays and celebrations in Portugal, and you compare them with traditions from your country. The goal is practical: understand the names of important days, say a simple wish, and ask how people celebrate.

- `O 25 de Abril é feriado nacional.` — “25 April is a national holiday.”
- `No Santo António, as pessoas comem sardinhas assadas.` — “On Saint Anthony’s Day, people eat grilled sardines.”
- `No Porto, as pessoas festejam o São João em junho.` — “In Porto, people celebrate Saint John in June.”
- `No Natal, muitas famílias comem bacalhau na consoada.` — “At Christmas, many families eat cod on Christmas Eve.”
- `Boas Festas!` / `Feliz Ano Novo!` — common wishes at the end of the year.
- `Como se festeja o Diwali no teu país?` — “How is Diwali celebrated in your country?”

Watch out:
- `feriado` is a public holiday; it is not the same as any party or festival.
- Contractions are very common: `no Natal`, `no Porto`, `na consoada`, `do 25 de Abril`.

exercises.explanation: This is a fixed wish used at the end of December and on 1 January.

exercises.explanation: Use «ser» to identify the day: «é feriado nacional».

exercises.explanation: For cities, use «em» with contraction where needed: «no Porto».

Em que mês se festeja o São João?

exercises.prompt: Your classmate says: «No meu país, festejamos o Diwali com a família.» Ask your classmate (informal) how Diwali is celebrated in their country.
exercises.explanation: You can learn «Como se festeja ... no teu país?» as a useful ready-made question.
exercises.givenAnswer: No meu país, festejamos o Diwali com a família.
acceptedAnswers: Como é que se festeja o Diwali no teu país?

exercises.explanation: Some items are general words and some are specific Portuguese traditions. Learn them as ready-made cultural words.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "Carnival is in February or March, depending on the year."
exercises.explanation: Carnaval changes date, so in Portugal it can be in February or in March.

exercises.explanation: Use «é» to define something. «De Natal» means it is connected with Christmas.

exercises.explanation: To ask about time, use «Quando (é que) ...?». Here the verb is impersonal: «se festeja».
